source: We know from previous publications that the use of an mGluR6b agonist drug can lead to monochromatic ERG defects that are stronger for short wavelength stimulation compared to the rest of the spectrum (Saszik et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Saszik et al., 2002.

claim: A higher concentration of mGluR6b in the dendritic terminals contacting UV cones could lead to stronger defects when blocked by an agonist.
source: It is possible that this defect would stem from a higher concentration of mGluR6b in the dendritic terminals contacting UV cones, consequently more affected by the block.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observed distribution patterns.

claim: EAAT5b and EAAT7 have different functions in the anisotropic larval retina.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that EAAT5b and EAAT7 have different functions in the anisotropic larval retina.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential distribution patterns observed.

claim: The different biophysical properties previously observed in EAAT5b and EAAT7 might aid the information acquisition for one or the other behavior.
source: This suggests that the different biophysical properties previously observed in EAAT5b and EAAT7 (Niklaus et al., 2024) might aid the information acquisition for one or the other behavior.
evidence: This is speculative inference based on the observed distribution and cited biophysical properties.

claim: UV cones residing in the nasal patch are relevant for predator avoidance.
source: Previous studies hypothesize that UV cones residing in the nasal patch are relevant for predator avoidance (Yoshimatsu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yoshimatsu et al., 2020.

claim: Zebrafish larvae strongly react to a virtual hunting stimulus in the UV wavelength range.
source: As expected, zebrafish larvae strongly react to a virtual hunting stimulus in the UV wavelength range (Figure 4B), but have very limited response to light targeting the middle-/long-wavelength cones (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: Zebrafish larvae have very limited response to light targeting the middle-/long-wavelength cones.
source: As expected, zebrafish larvae strongly react to a virtual hunting stimulus in the UV wavelength range (Figure 4B), but have very limited response to light targeting the middle-/long-wavelength cones (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Larvae showed an initial higher response to UV stimuli, waning off by the 10th repetition, probably due to stimulus habituation.
source: Interestingly, larvae showed an initial higher response, waning off by the 10th repetition, probably due to stimulus habituation.
evidence: This is observed from behavioral data and interpreted as habituation.

claim: The number of recorded hunting responses steadily increased along with the stimulus strength from intensity 40%, reaching a plateau around intensity 70%.
source: Following our expectation, the number of recorded hunting responses steadily increased along with the stimulus strength from intensity 40%, reaching a plateau around intensity 70%.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: WT larvae can generally detect the UV stimulus starting from 40% of intensity.
source: Moreover, we could demonstrate that number of responses is dependent on the stimulus intensity and that with our setup, WT larvae can generally detect the stimulus starting from 40% of intensity.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data.

claim: Both EAAT5b and EAAT7 are expressed at the dendritic tips of UV cones, being concentrated in the SZ and in the nasal patch, respectively.
source: Whole mount retina imaging shows that both EAAT5b and EAAT7 are expressed at the dendritic tips of UV cones, being concentrated in the SZ and in the nasal patch, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in the manuscript.

claim: KO of both eaat5b and eaat7 leads to a reduced b-wave in larvae stimulated with short wavelength light.
source: Monochromatic ERG recordings show that KO of both eaat5b and eaat7 leads to a reduced b-wave in larvae stimulated with short wavelength light.
evidence: This is supported by ERG data presented in the manuscript.

claim: WT fish (4%) can react to the UV stimulus already with 30% of LED intensity.
source: Our experiments show that even if scarcely (4%), WT larvae can react to the UV stimulus already with 30% of LED intensity (Figure 5A), while mutants lacking EAAT5b start responding from intensity at 40% (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Mutants lacking EAAT5b start responding to UV stimulus from intensity at 40%.
source: Our experiments show that even if scarcely (4%), WT larvae can react to the UV stimulus already with 30% of LED intensity (Figure 5A), while mutants lacking EAAT5b start responding from intensity at 40% (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: WT larvae have a stimulus detections success of 44% at 80% intensity.
source: While the response peak is reached in both genotypes at 80% intensity, WT larvae have a stimulus detections success of 44% (Figure 5A), eaat5b-/- mutants show a lower response (35%) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: eaat5b-/- mutants show a lower response (35%) at 80% intensity.
source: While the response peak is reached in both genotypes at 80% intensity, WT larvae have a stimulus detections success of 44% (Figure 5A), eaat5b-/- mutants show a lower response (35%) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Light-intensity-specific comparison between eaat5b-/- mutants and WT animals did not indicate any significant difference.
source: Surprisingly, light-intensity-specific comparison between eaat5b-/- mutants and WT animals did not indicate any significant difference (Chi-square test p-value >0.05 in every instance).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of behavioral data.

claim: The comparison of the proportion between successful hunting responses over total stimuli through the whole test did not result in a significant difference between eaat5b-/- mutants and WT.
source: Similarly, neither the comparison of the proportion between successful hunting responses over total stimuli through the whole test, nor the one between responses distributions across the intensity levels resulted in a significant difference (two proportions z-test p-value: 0.16; Kolmogorov-Smirnov test p-value: 0.83) (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: eaat7 mutants displayed overall better responses when compared to the WT larvae in the UV hunting assay.
source: Interestingly, eaat7 mutants (n=19) displayed overall better responses when compared to the WT larvae (n=18) (Figure 6 right panel).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 6.

claim: WT larvae could detect the UV stimulus from intensity 30% (~5%).
source: While the latter could still detect the stimulus from intensity 30% (~5%) (Figure 6A left), eaat7-/- fish started reacting to UV from intensity 20% (~5%) (Figure 6B left panel).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: eaat7-/- fish started reacting to UV from intensity 20% (~5%).
source: While the latter could still detect the stimulus from intensity 30% (~5%) (Figure 6A left), eaat7-/- fish started reacting to UV from intensity 20% (~5%) (Figure 6B left panel).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Response peak is reached at 60% for the WT controls with a response of 33%.
source: Response peak is reached at 60% for the controls and between 80 and 90% for the mutants; with WT larvae with a response of 33% while eaat7 mutants reach 53% of response (Figure 6 left panel).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 6.

claim: eaat7 mutants reach 53% of response at peak (between 80 and 90% intensity).
source: Response peak is reached at 60% for the controls and between 80 and 90% for the mutants; with WT larvae with a response of 33% while eaat7 mutants reach 53% of response (Figure 6 left panel).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 6.

claim: WT animals performed less than eaat7 mutants did when comparing pooled responses over the total of delivered stimuli (two proportions z-test p-value: 0.0011).
source: By comparing pooled responses over the total of delivered stimuli, we discovered that WT animals performed less than eaat7 mutants did (two proportions z-test p-value: 0.0011; Figure 6C left panel).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The comparison of intensity-specific responses distributions between WT and eaat7 mutants led to no significant difference (Kolmogorov-Smirnov test p-value: 0.17).
source: Conversely, the comparison of intensity-specific responses distributions led to no significant difference (Kolmogorov-Smirnov test p-value: 0.17) (Figure 6C right panel).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Lack or presence of both the postsynaptic EAATs might impact response to UV light and prey capture.
source: Taken together, our assay shows that lack or presence of both the postsynaptic EAATs might impact response to UV light and prey capture and, interestingly, the lack of EAAT7 appears to facilitate prey detection.
evidence: This is inferred from the behavioral assay results.

claim: The lack of EAAT7 appears to facilitate prey detection.
source: Taken together, our assay shows that lack or presence of both the postsynaptic EAATs might impact response to UV light and prey capture and, interestingly, the lack of EAAT7 appears to facilitate prey detection.
evidence: This is inferred from the behavioral assay results showing increased responses in eaat7 mutants.

claim: EAAT5b and EAAT7 have different gating dynamics along with different chloride current generation capacity.
source: Previous studies from our group (Niklaus et al., 2024) show that EAAT5b and EAAT7 have different gating dynamics along with different chloride current generation capacity.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Niklaus et al., 2024.

claim: The lack of one or the other factor changes signal responses and information integration in important areas such as the SZ, thus altering the larva's ability to detect and respond to a prey stimulus.
source: Hence, it is conceivable that the lack of one or the other factor changes signal responses and information integration in important areas such as the SZ, thus altering the larva's ability to detect and respond to a prey stimulus.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observed behavioral differences.

claim: eaat5b mutants show a marked reduction on the time spent swimming towards the stimulus, particularly at the higher contrasts (contrast: 213; p=0.01).
source: As expected, eaat5b mutants show a marked reduction on the time spent swimming towards the stimulus, particularly at the higher contrasts (contrast: 213; p=0.01) (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by OMR assay data shown in Figure 7C with statistical significance.

claim: eaat7-/- fish do not show any visible defect in OMR when compared with WT even if monochromatic ERG data showed a marked decrease in their b-wave.
source: Interestingly, eaat7-/- fish do not show any visible defect when compared with WT even if monochromatic ERG data showed a marked decrease in their b-wave.
evidence: This is supported by OMR assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Both mutants increase overall movement in a contrast-dependent trend with no significant differences from the respective WT control groups.
source: Both mutants increase overall movement in a contrast-dependent trend with no significant differences from the respective WT control groups (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by OMR assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The optomotor response draws information from both the ON and OFF pathway.
source: The optomotor response draws information from both the ON and OFF pathway, and it is conceivable that removing EAAT7 would not generate a defect large enough to be measured by our assay.
evidence: This is established knowledge about OMR.

claim: Removing EAAT7 would not generate a defect large enough to be measured by the OMR assay.
source: The optomotor response draws information from both the ON and OFF pathway, and it is conceivable that removing EAAT7 would not generate a defect large enough to be measured by our assay.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning to explain the lack of observed defect.

claim: The loss of EAAT5b and EAAT7 reduces ON-bipolar cell responses.
source: Our previous studies demonstrated that the loss of EAAT5b and EAAT7 reduces ON-bipolar cell responses, with eaat5b mutants being less affected than eaat5b/eaat7 double mutants, which also exhibit altered response kinetics (Niklaus et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Niklaus et al., 2024.

claim: eaat5b mutants are less affected than eaat5b/eaat7 double mutants.
source: Our previous studies demonstrated that the loss of EAAT5b and EAAT7 reduces ON-bipolar cell responses, with eaat5b mutants being less affected than eaat5b/eaat7 double mutants, which also exhibit altered response kinetics (Niklaus et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Niklaus et al., 2024.

claim: eaat5b/eaat7 double mutants exhibit altered response kinetics.
source: Our previous studies demonstrated that the loss of EAAT5b and EAAT7 reduces ON-bipolar cell responses, with eaat5b mutants being less affected than eaat5b/eaat7 double mutants, which also exhibit altered response kinetics (Niklaus et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Niklaus et al., 2024.

claim: A lack of EAAT5b and EAAT7 leads to modest reductions in the ON-response under UV-blue and red light.
source: We found that a lack of EAAT5b and EAAT7 leads to modest reductions in the ON-response under UV-blue and red light.
evidence: This is supported by ERG data presented in the manuscript.

claim: No reduced responses were observed under green illumination in eaat5b and eaat7 mutants.
source: Interestingly, we did not observe any reduced responses under green illumination, suggesting a spectral-specific role in modulation by these proteins.
evidence: This is supported by ERG data presented in the manuscript.

claim: EAAT5b and EAAT7 have a spectral-specific role in modulation.
source: Interestingly, we did not observe any reduced responses under green illumination, suggesting a spectral-specific role in modulation by these proteins.
evidence: This is inferred from the wavelength-specific ERG defects.

claim: Due to the strong overlap of UV and blue cones' light sensitivities, whole retina recordings with a wide-field stimulus cannot separate these two channels.
source: However, due to the strong overlap of UV and blue cones' light sensitivities, our whole retina recordings with a wide-field stimulus cannot separate these two channels (Yoshimatsu et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yoshimatsu et al., 2021.

claim: Recent studies have uncovered a complex anisotropy of the larval zebrafish eye, matched to the visual ecology that they live in.
source: Recent studies have uncovered a complex anisotropy of the larval zebrafish eye, matched to the visual ecology that they live in Zimmermann et al., 2018.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zimmermann et al., 2018.

claim: EAAT5b and EAAT7 are largely co-expressed at most dendritic tips.
source: In line with previous data, we observed that EAAT5b and EAAT7 are largely co-expressed at most dendritic tips (Niklaus et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data and citation to Niklaus et al., 2024.

claim: EAAT7 is highest expressed in ventral regions of the retina with an intensity drop at the area temporalis or the strike zone (SZ).
source: EAAT7 is highest expressed in ventral regions of the retina with an intensity drop at the area temporalis or the strike zone (SZ).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in the manuscript.

claim: EAAT5b's signal is elevated in the strike zone, where the highest concentration of UV cones is also found.
source: Conversely, EAAT5b's signal is elevated in this specific area, where the highest concentration of UV cones is also found.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The peculiar localization of Eaat5b in the SZ, along with the observed defect in the UV/Blue range upon KO, suggests an involvement of Eaat5b in prey detection and capture.
source: The peculiar localization of Eaat5b in the SZ, along with the observed defect in the UV/Blue range upon KO, suggests an involvement of Eaat5b in prey detection and capture.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined localization and functional data.

claim: Hunting behavior has been extensively studied in the past years, both using live paramecia and virtual assays.
source: Hunting behavior has been extensively studied in the past years, both using live paramecia (Semmelhack et al., 2014; Yoshimatsu et al., 2020) and virtual assays (Bianco et al., 2011; Semmelhack et al., 2014), where generally a moving white dot is projected on a screen and displayed to a larva.
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Responses to UV light were significantly more frequent than those to yellow light in WT fish.
source: We validated the setup by testing WT fish reactions to yellow and UV light, first confirming that responses to UV light were significantly more frequent than those to yellow light, and second, that the UV response rate was directly proportional to light intensity.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The UV response rate was directly proportional to light intensity.
source: We validated the setup by testing WT fish reactions to yellow and UV light, first confirming that responses to UV light were significantly more frequent than those to yellow light, and second, that the UV response rate was directly proportional to light intensity.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: No significant effect on prey-detection and capture behavior was observed in the Eaat5b mutants.
source: Surprisingly, we did not observe a significant effect on prey-detection and capture behavior in the Eaat5b mutants, while Eaat7 mutants showed an increased response rate and a lower threshold than WT fish.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Eaat7 mutants showed an increased response rate and a lower threshold than WT fish in the UV hunting assay.
source: Surprisingly, we did not observe a significant effect on prey-detection and capture behavior in the Eaat5b mutants, while Eaat7 mutants showed an increased response rate and a lower threshold than WT fish.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Removal of Eaat5b leads to a shortening of the time to peak of the measured b-waves.
source: Namely, removal of Eaat5b leads to a shortening of the time to peak of the measured b-waves, while Eaat7 causes a lengthening of the same, indicating opposing roles in regulating the ON-BCs depolarization timing (Niklaus et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Niklaus et al., 2024.

claim: Eaat7 causes a lengthening of the time to peak of the measured b-waves.
source: Namely, removal of Eaat5b leads to a shortening of the time to peak of the measured b-waves, while Eaat7 causes a lengthening of the same, indicating opposing roles in regulating the ON-BCs depolarization timing (Niklaus et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Niklaus et al., 2024.

claim: EAAT5b and EAAT7 have opposing roles in regulating the ON-BCs depolarization timing.
source: Namely, removal of Eaat5b leads to a shortening of the time to peak of the measured b-waves, while Eaat7 causes a lengthening of the same, indicating opposing roles in regulating the ON-BCs depolarization timing (Niklaus et al., 2024).
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects on b-wave kinetics.

claim: UV-cones in the SZ have longer signal integration compared to the other photoreceptors, supposedly to better track a moving prey.
source: UV-cones in the SZ have longer signal integration compared to the other photoreceptors, supposedly to better track a moving prey (Yoshimatsu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yoshimatsu et al., 2020.

claim: The concentration of Eaat5b in the BC terminals of the SZ might be another mechanism to slow down the signal and facilitate prey tracking behavior.
source: The concentration of Eaat5b in the BC terminals of this region might be another mechanism to slow down the signal and facilitate this behavior.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observed localization and kinetics.

claim: Loss of Eaat5b might result in a reduced prey-tracking ability.
source: Loss of Eaat5b might then result in a reduced prey-tracking ability; while conversely, the absence of a functional Eaat7 could lead to slower integration times throughout the whole retina, consequently making stimulus sensitivity higher.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observed kinetics and behavioral results.

claim: The absence of a functional Eaat7 could lead to slower integration times throughout the whole retina, consequently making stimulus sensitivity higher.
source: Loss of Eaat5b might then result in a reduced prey-tracking ability; while conversely, the absence of a functional Eaat7 could lead to slower integration times throughout the whole retina, consequently making stimulus sensitivity higher.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observed kinetics and behavioral results.

claim: OMR is driven by both ON- and OFF-stimuli.
source: Since OMR is driven by both ON- and OFF-stimuli (Orger and Baier, 2005; Kist and Portugues, 2019) and zebrafish larvae typically respond equally to both contrast changes when their field of view is restricted (as in our assay), it is possible that any impairment in the ON-response was compensated by the larvae's strong reaction to light-dark transitions.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Orger and Baier, 2005 and Kist and Portugues, 2019.

claim: Zebrafish larvae typically respond equally to both contrast changes when their field of view is restricted.
source: Since OMR is driven by both ON- and OFF-stimuli (Orger and Baier, 2005; Kist and Portugues, 2019) and zebrafish larvae typically respond equally to both contrast changes when their field of view is restricted (as in our assay), it is possible that any impairment in the ON-response was compensated by the larvae's strong reaction to light-dark transitions.
evidence: This is established knowledge about zebrafish OMR behavior.

claim: Any impairment in the ON-response in eaat7 mutants was possibly compensated by the larvae's strong reaction to light-dark transitions.
source: Since OMR is driven by both ON- and OFF-stimuli (Orger and Baier, 2005; Kist and Portugues, 2019) and zebrafish larvae typically respond equally to both contrast changes when their field of view is restricted (as in our assay), it is possible that any impairment in the ON-response was compensated by the larvae's strong reaction to light-dark transitions.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning to explain the lack of observed defect in eaat7 mutants.

claim: Both Eaat5b and Eaat7 transcripts are expressed throughout the brain.
source: Both Eaat5b and Eaat7 transcripts are expressed throughout the brain (Niklaus et al., 2024), and both localization and effects of their loss in the zebrafish brain are yet to be investigated.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Niklaus et al., 2024.

claim: Both localization and effects of Eaat5b and Eaat7 loss in the zebrafish brain are yet to be investigated.
source: Both Eaat5b and Eaat7 transcripts are expressed throughout the brain (Niklaus et al., 2024), and both localization and effects of their loss in the zebrafish brain are yet to be investigated.
evidence: This acknowledges a gap in current knowledge.

claim: While mGluR6b remains the main regulator of ON-BCs depolarization throughout the retina, Eaat5b and Eaat7 modulate response speeds in different regions of the retina to optimize behavior-specific integration dynamics, particularly in relation to UV light.
source: Taken together, our data suggests that while mGluR6b remains the main regulator of ON-BCs depolarization throughout the retina, Eaat5b and Eaat7 modulate response speeds in different regions of the retina to optimize behavior-specific integration dynamics, particularly in relation to UV light.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data in the manuscript.
